as_told.title: Vallée's Passport to Magonia: the same phenomenon wearing cultural masks
as_told.place_text: Europe; Celtic lands; Ellsworth missile base, South Dakota

plain: This story is about a book called Passport to Magonia by an author and researcher named Jacques Vallee. According to the people who describe it, Vallee compared old folk tales about fairies and elves with modern reports of meetings with aliens. A writer on ancient history, Graham Hancock, says the old stories sound very like the new ones: fairies and elves who abducted people, did surgery on them, had sex with them and produced hybrid babies. He also links this to another book called Supernatural. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, tells it too, in his own words. He calls Passport to Magonia a great book whose argument annoyed both believers and doubters. In his telling, it is one phenomenon wearing different cultural masks over the centuries, and he applies the idea to a 1977 case at Ellsworth, an Air Force base in South Dakota. If the comparison holds, then today's alien encounters would be the latest form of something people have described for a very long time.
